blocks.text: LESSON 1
JESUS WAS HUMAN
Scripture Texts: Isaiah 7:14; Matthew 1:1; Galatians 4:4; 1 Timothy 2:5; Hebrews 4:15; 1 John 4:2-3; Romans 8:3-4

No greater subject can occupy our thoughts than consideration of the Lord Jesus Christ. We finite beings can never exhaust the knowledge of an infinite Being. The Bible provides endless studies of Him. In this quarterly, we will give attention to only a small portion of these. Reverent con-sideration of these truths of Jesus should stir feelings of attraction and belief and lead on to acts of love, worship, submission, and obedience. Christ has two sides to His identity. Today we consider one side—His humanity. In the next lesson, we will consider the other side—His divinity.
MEMORY VERSE: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh. —Romans 8:3
Jesus Had a Fleshly Birth

Isaiah 7:14 A virgin shall conceive. This prophecy was given at least seven hundred years before Jesus was born, His mother being a virgin and His Father being God. Thus, the Son would have one human and one divine parent. He was God joined with man in one body—"Emmanuel," meaning "God with us" (Matthew 1:23).

Matthew 1:1 The son of David, the son of Abraham. Jesus was born in-to the human family. He descended through Mary from Abraham and David. He is the promised Son of David whose "kingdom" is to be "for ever" (2 Samuel 7:12-13).

Galatians 4:4 At the time planned by God, Jesus was made of a woman, just as all humans are. Through His mother, He had every human nature and attribute. Christ, the Son of God, became truly human. This had to be if He was to make atonement for human sins. We must believe in and accept Him as such to be saved.
Jesus, the Mediator
1 Timothy 2:5 One mediator between God and men, the man Christ

Jesus. Being God, He reached God. Being man, He reached men. God and men came together in Christ. As finite humans, we must connect with the Infinite. Without Him, we are lost, without hope, nothing certain, no goal, and no truth or light to guide us. Only in Him Who is all wisdom, all goodness, and all love can our needs be supplied. He is the only point at which we may reach God (John 14:6). Be not deceived—good works, suffering, sacrifice, Mary worship, preachers, organizations, or forms of worship cannot bring us to God. Only One can, the man Christ Jesus.

Sin separates man from God. Sin brought spiritual death to all mankind. The only atonement for sin is the death of the sinner. "The soul that sinneth, it shall die" (Ezekiel 18:4). The only escape from this end for any man is for another man to die in his place. Only a man can take a man's place. One sinner cannot atone for another because his own sin requires all the payment his death could make. God yearned for the fellowship of His created children. The only way to free them was for God to become man and die in their place. This He did in Jesus Christ. The divine-human Jesus tasted "death for every man" (Hebrews 2:9) to bring them into fellowship with God.

Hebrews 4:15 When in need, in trouble, or guilty, we want someone who understands us, who sympathizes and cares. Jesus is that One. He is touched with the feeling of our infirmities. Being human, He was in all points tempted, and He understands. Being love, He cares. Being all power, He can help, as He is able to do all things. His humanity reaches our need. His divinity supplies the remedy. Praise God! He came all the way down to our level.
A Test of Spirits

1 John 4:2-3 In these days of many doctrines differing from the true standard, we need an immovable standard by which to judge them. Here it is. Ask, "Does this doctrine teach that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh?" That is, was God actually present in the man, Jesus Christ? If the spirit of a teaching answers yes, it is of God and built on a true foundation. If it denies the union of God and man in Christ, it is not of God. Avoid this spirit of antichrist. A denial of the Virgin Birth is simply a denial of this union in Jesus (1 John 2:22-23; John 1:1, 14).
Christ's Work in Man
Romans 8:3-4 What the law could not do .... The Law gave God's standard of life to man, but man could not live up to it. Why not? Because

the law left the performance of it resting upon man's strength and ability, upon the flesh. God knew man could not live holy in his human strength and gave the Law to teach him that fact. He wants us to depend upon His strength. This is why God sent his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh. Jesus lived a perfect, holy life. Looking at Him, men see their sinfulness and feel condemnation. Following this conviction with repentance brings cleansing of the sin. Then, if we continue to walk after the Spirit—in complete obedience to Him—the righteousness of the law is fulfilled in us. This is the purpose of Jesus Christ's incarnation—the coming of God into human flesh.
JUST A THOUGHT
Sinful thoughts will rise, but never let them reign.

blocks.text: LESSON 2
JESUS WAS DIVINE
Scripture Text: John 1:1-10, 14

Who is Jesus? Everything in our lives depends upon whether we know the true answer to this question. "By him all things consist" (Colossians 1:17). "In him we live, and move, and have our being" (Acts 17:28). Whatever He is, we are. If He falls, we fall. Our life, both physical and spiritual, depends upon Him. If He is just another human, we have no support and are without hope. If He is divine, we have all the strength to support us in living a victorious life and having the hope of Heaven. By examining some qualities of Jesus recorded in the Bible, we can find who He is.
MEMORY VERSE: For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bod-ily. —Colossians 2:9
In the Beginning

John 1:1-2 In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God. The beginning is as far back as we can go. Jesus' life did not begin when He was born as a baby. He had always lived with God His Father. He is "from everlasting to everlasting" (Psalm 90:2; 106:48). He is alive forever-more. He can never die again (Revelation 1:18; Romans 6:9). This eternally existing One is called the Word. He is the living Word and is greater than the written Word, the Bible, because He produced it. He is God's message to us. God could trust no other (Hebrews 1:1-6). The Word was God. Jesus was God in the flesh, sent to live among those whom He had created. He was of the same substance and nature as His Father.

John 1:3 All things were made by him. (See also Colossians 1:16.) Only the omniscient and omnipotent One has the knowledge and power required to create all things and operate them. All power and knowledge belongs to Jesus.
Jesus Is Life-Giving

John 1:4 In him was life. We, too, have life, but ours is borrowed life. We have no power over our lives. His is His own (John 5:26). He could lay His down or "take it again" (John 10:18). Jesus not only possessed life, but

to those who would ask it, He said, "I give unto them eternal life" (John 10:28). Here we see the necessity of our having a Savior Who is divine. No one but God can give life to a dead soul. Only as Jesus Christ is God can He save us.
Jesus Is the Light

John 1:4-5 The life was the light of men. The only light that would be able to shine into and enlighten the hearts of men. And the light shineth in darkness—as He dispelled darkness with light in the beginning of creation, He dispels darkness in the soul of man when He shines His light into their lives darkened by sin. Darkness comprehended it not. Satan, the ruler over the kingdom of darkness, cannot comprehend it.

John 1:9-10 That was the true light. Light is truth, and truth is light. Without Christ our souls are in darkness. Christ sends light to show us the right way and lead us out of darkness. His light is given to every man. Not every man walks in it, but it shines for him if only he will turn his eyes toward it. How the world needs light! Blindly, the great multitudes turn from Jesus now as when He came two thousand years ago, ignorant of their loss. Walking in darkness, they reject their only hope of salvation. They fail to see Him as their Creator and Savior.
Believing Is the Key

John 1:14 The Word was made flesh. Here is proof that the Word is the same One born as the human baby Jesus. Jesus is divine. He is Deity. Jesus is the Man who lived, died, and rose again in Palestine. He is truly God. To believe this is necessary for salvation. Jesus said, "I am from above .... if ye believe not that I am he, ye shall die in your sins" (John 8:23-24). To believe on Him as such is more than head knowledge. It begins there, goes on in faith, and continues in the action of casting ourselves into His keeping. We do not truly believe until we trust Him.

If someone tells you Jesus was only a man subject to limits and faults as we are, turn from him as a false teacher. As Jesus walked these shores, taught the people, and healed the sick, He was God moving about as a man. We beheld his glory. No doubt when John wrote this, his mind envisioned Jesus clothed in heavenly beauty on the mount before him and Peter and James. But glimpses of His glory were always being shown forth as supplies of grace and truth. These brought from Peter the testimony, "And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God"
(John 6:69). This same belief and testimony flow from the heart of every sinner as he becomes a saint. By His grace, Jesus reveals God's love; by His truth, He reveals God's light.

Notice in the memory verse that no quality or power possessed by any of the Trinity is lacking in Jesus. He has all the fulness—in abundance. Bodily—present in His body, in His person. He could say, "I am in the Father, and the Father in me" (John 14:10).
JUST A THOUGHT
Can we fathom the grief of Christ who came to bless only to be repulsed by those He made and loves?

blocks.text: LESSON 3
JESUS WAS PERFECT
Scripture Texts: 1 Corinthians 8:6; John 10:17-18; Hebrews 7:26; Colos-sians 1:19; Matthew 5:48

We have seen Jesus is both human and divine. In His humanity, He draws near to us in a common feeling. We understand more about this side of His personality since we share human experiences. On the other hand, His divinity may seem further away and be more difficult for us to understand. The quality of perfection brings the two together and helps us to understand what is included in Jesus for mankind. Let us look in the Bible for some help on the meaning of godly perfection.
MEMORY VERSE: Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect. —Matthew 5:48
A Perfect Creator and Ruler

1 Corinthians 8:6 Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things. We look at one who studies a single line of knowledge until he becomes an expert and call him a genius. Yet he may have only scratched the surface on that subject. Now consider the One by whom are all things. ALL, not one line only. It took a perfect Creator to bring about a perfect creation. All creation depends upon His perfect rule. The sun and planets move at His direction. Man sets time by them. Ships are guided and kept on their course by them. All things obey His natural laws perfectly. And we by him. Our life, breath, thought, motions, and complete existence depend on Him for perfect operation. "In him we live, and move, and have our being" (Acts 17:28).

Jesus Christ possesses "all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge" (Colossians 2:3). He did not learn knowledge—He made it—and wisdom, the ability to use knowledge in the best way. Jesus is Master of these. By them He made the worlds. By them He rules. He created perfectly. He rules perfectly. He does all in unity with the Father and the Spirit.
A Perfect Salvation
John 10:17-18 Jesus has power over His own life. He can lay it down and take it again. He exercised that power at His Crucifixion and Resurrec-

tion. No one took Jesus' life; He gave it. To give it was His purpose in coming (Matthew 20:28). Jesus lived a perfect life, and only through Him are our lives made perfect. Not perfection in the eyes of men, but perfect in doing the will of God (Hebrews 13:20-21). He is "alive for evermore" (Revelation 1:18). Jesus can say, "I am ... the life" (John 11:25). Jesus has eternal life, and He can give eternal spiritual life. There is no greater mark of perfection than this. Jesus can give perfect victory over every foe who would rob us of this eternal life. If we stay in His hand, no enemy can remove us.

Perfect salvation is not partial—saving a man from some sins and leaving him in others. It does not remove the punishment while leaving the sin. Perfect salvation is not that which some of the church world is teaching, that Christians sin, that simply believing on Christ brings forgiveness of both past and future sins, and that Christ cannot give us power to keep from sinning (Jude 24).

Christ's death did not atone for only part of our sins and leave us to atone for the rest by suffering in purgatory. You cannot fall so low as to be beyond the power of Christ to save. Salvation reaches as deep as the stain of sin has gone (Isaiah 1:18). "He is able also to save them to the uttermost"—to the fullest extent—all who "come unto God by him" (Hebrews 7:25). All who come believing Him, who repent of sin and trust Him—this is the only way. It is a perfect salvation, cleansing from all sin here and providing a deathless body hereafter.
A Perfect Holiness

Hebrews 7:26 Christ was never stained by sin. He had perfect victory over every temptation. Both His acts and His Words are holy because He is holy ("no sin"; 1 Peter 2:22). He is higher than the heavens. Holiness is more than the absence of sin. It is the presence of perfect godliness, the quality of God. Godliness is the predominating ingredient of holiness, since it is the producer of sinlessness. Being perfect is holiness. Only Christ has power to make us holy. Only holy people can dwell with Him.

Colossians 1:19 In him should all fulness dwell. In Christ are all the qualities of God in their fullest or perfect extent. Perfect wisdom, perfect power, perfect love, perfect mercy, the list is endless. Possessing these does not make Him perfect. He possesses them because He is perfect.

It pleased the Father that His Son should have all fulness, a complete and perfect God. The Father's pleasure in this shows the love and unity that exist among the Trinity, binding Father, Son, and the Holy Spirit into one
perfect unit.

Matthew 5:48 Be ye therefore perfect. This is of great value to us. A perfect Savior laid a perfect sacrifice on God's altar. That perfect sacrifice bought a perfect salvation. His perfect love brought it all to pass and ob-tained a perfect way for all sinners to have a perfect hope to be saved now and eternally.
JUST A THOUGHT
Perfection is not reaching a human goal in life but faithfulness in serving the Lord.

JESUS WAS A PROPHET
Scripture Texts: Deuteronomy 18:18-22; John 7:37-40; 12:48-50

Foretelling future events is only one phase of prophecy. Whenever a per-son speaks a message given him by the Holy Spirit, it is prophecy, and he is a prophet. The message may be doctrine, reproof, instruction, comfort, warning, or prediction of coming events. If it comes directly from God to His servant who speaks, it is prophecy.

Jesus came from God the Father, spoke the words of the Father, and did the works of the Father. He was a specially chosen Prophet of God. We must obey every word He has spoken for this will judge us at the Final Judgment.
MEMORY VERSE: And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the High-est: for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways. —Luke 1:76
The Promise of a Prophet

Deuteronomy 18:18-19 When God met Moses on Mount Sinai to give to Israel His Law, the people waiting below were frightened by the manifes-tation of God in thunderings, lightnings, loud trumpet, and the mountain smoking. They asked that God not speak to them directly, "lest we die" (Exodus 20:18-19). God promised a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee—like Moses, a man. Whosoever will not hearken ... he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him. Disobedience to the words of this Prophet would bring guilt and severe punishment. Why? Because the words of this Prophet would be the words of God.
Marks of a Prophet

Deuteronomy 18:20-22 False prophets will come. Shall die—the penalty for falsely prophesying was death. But many, possibly thousands, would be misled by those deceivers before judgment came. God gave Israel a measuring rod: the words of a true prophet would come to pass.
The marks of a true prophet are:
(1) A true prophet of God comes from God.
(2) He speaks the words of God.
(3) His prophecy comes to pass.

Are there any "false prophets" among the people today? Jesus said there would be (Matthew 24:24), and Peter wrote that there would be (2 Peter 2:1). Yes, they may be found close to all of us. By the following test, we can distinguish the false from the true:
(1) Is he sent by God?
(2) Does his life manifest the spirit and graces of a follower of Jesus?
(3) Does he speak the words of God? Since all truth agrees, the words and spirit of a true prophet must agree with the Word of God, the Bible.
(4) Do his words come to pass? Do his teachings produce godly re-sults?
(5) Are his prayers answered?
To judge between false and true prophets, two things are of utmost importance:
(1) A knowledge of God's Word.
(2) An indwelling of the Holy Spirit.
Jesus Prophesied

John 7:37-40 Around 1500 years after God promised to send a Prophet, Jesus came to earth and taught. He said, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. He gives a supply that satisfies those who receive it and overflows to satisfy others (John 4:10-14). He that believeth on me ... shall flow rivers of living water. Here it is again, the great results of believing on Christ. "All things are possible to him that believeth" (Mark 9:23). "Whoso-ever believeth in him should not perish" (John 3:15). "He that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live" (John 11:25).

Much is included in what God calls believing. Belief brings action (but this spake he of the Spirit). Only saved people, those cleansed from sin and born anew, can receive the Holy Spirit when they open their hearts to Him and yield all to His rule. Of a truth this is the Prophet. Many remembered the promise from years before and believed. He was speaking the words from God.
The Standard of Judgment

John 12:48 The word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day. Revelation 20:12 tells what the Judgment is based on: "And the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books [plural], according to their works." These "books" are the Books of the Ages that governed the various times in which man lived. People who lived prior to the New Testament dispensation are not held to the standard of greater New Testament light we enjoy today. God judges with a true and just weight, based on what was available and what they did with what was available to them in their day.
If our name is "not found written in the book of life," we will have fallen short of God's standard. "The second death" will be our sad end (Revelation 20:14-15).

John 12:49-50 I have not spoken of myself; but the Father which sent me, he gave me a commandment, what I should say ... his commandment is life everlasting. Jesus had all the marks of a true prophet of God:
(1) Jesus was sent by God.
(2) Jesus spoke the words of God.
(3) The words Jesus spoke were truth—life everlasting.
All the promises of Jesus have proven true. All His predictions have come to pass so far, and we believe the rest will as well. Jesus left no doubt that He is the Prophet God promised to send.

Jesus is the Mediator between God and man. He is the representative of God to man and the representative of man to God. When He represents God to man, He is a Prophet. When He represents man before God, He is a Priest.
JUST A THOUGHT
To return evil for good is devilish; to return good for good is human; to return good for evil is godly.

blocks.text: LESSON 5
JESUS WAS A PRIEST
Scripture Text: Hebrews 8:1-10

Being the Mediator set between God and man, Jesus reaches both ways. He is the Prophet representing God to man. He is the Priest representing man to God. Both are required to accomplish our salvation.

Christ is our High Priest offering Himself to God as the Supreme Sacri-fice to pay for our sins and interceding with God for us. We must accept Him as our Sacrifice and Intercessor. Today we study His priesthood. (Read Hebrews, Chapter 9.)
MEMORY VERSE: Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profes-sion. —Hebrews 4:14
The Superiority of Christ's Priesthood

Hebrews 8:1-2 Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: the writer had been telling about the Levitical priesthood in Chapter 7. He told how another priest would rise up and that the priesthood being changed would cause a change to be necessary in the Law. This priest would bring in a more powerful and unchangeable priesthood. He ties up the loose ends and comes to a clear conclusion—we have such an high priest. Though we have sinned, by faith, we have a Spokesman who presents our case before the Father. This pathway to God was opened when Jesus suffered and shed His blood for us on Calvary.

When Jesus died, the Veil of the Temple was rent in two, breaking "down the middle wall of partition," opening the way between the people and the holiest place (Ephesians 2:13-16). No more would man need to go to God through a carnal priest but would draw nigh to God through this high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne ... in the heavens.

Our Priest sits where He can present our case directly. He serves in the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle. This is not a material building built by man. It is the sanctuary of the heart where God dwells, the tabernacle set up by the Lord ... and not man. "Jesus Christ" is our "advocate with the Father" (1 John 2:1).
Jesus the High Priest

Hebrews 8:3 Israel under the Law had priests and high priests. Priests kept the altar fire burning, offered sacrifices, kept oil in the golden candle-stick, changed the shewbread, and offered incense on the altar. They taught God's Law to the people and prayed for them.

The high priest was above the regular priests. He alone was allowed to enter the holiest place, and that but once a year. No man was to be in the holy place (the first room of the Tabernacle) when the high priest was in the holiest place (the inner room). High priests under the Law were types of the perfect High Priest, Jesus Christ. The sacrifices they offered were types of the perfect sacrifice of Himself that Jesus would offer.
The Old Covenant

Hebrews 8:4-9 The material Tabernacle and furniture, the sacrifices, the forms and ceremonies of the Law, all were earthly types of heavenly things. This is why it was so necessary that Moses make every detail of the tabernacle ... according to the pattern God showed him. The type must give a true picture.

Earth had sufficient human priests. Their service was an example and shadow, or a type of heavenly things, and not the reality of them. "For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins" (Hebrews 10:4). The need was too great. A better sacrifice, a better system than the Law was necessary. The Law was faulty. It could not bring salva-tion—only point to it. Then Jesus came, fulfilling the Law in a more ex-cellent ministry. He brought a better covenant and better promises.
The New Covenant

Hebrews 8:10 The better covenant Jesus made was: I will put my laws into their mind, And write them in their hearts. Through the new birth, He would change men's hearts and minds to think as He thinks and desire what He desires. He gave them His "divine nature" (2 Peter 1:4). He gave the Holy Spirit to instruct and guide them. In this new covenant, God and His people are joined in love and fellowship. Jesus sealed the new covenant with His own "blood" (Matthew 26:28). He offered Himself as the pure and living Sacrifice to bind it.
When Jesus ascended to Heaven, He entered the true Holy of Holies. There as High Priest, He meets the Father and pleads our case. There His

sacrifice is accepted as payment for our debt. There "he ever liveth to make intercession for them ... that come unto God by him" (Hebrews 7:25). We must hold fast our profession, as the memory verse states. It remains only for us to trust in the payment and intercession Jesus made for us. Keep trusting, obeying, praying, and communing with Him.
JUST A THOUGHT
Jesus was God brought down to man so that man could be lifted up to God.

blocks.text: LESSON 6
JESUS IS OUR ATONEMENT
Scripture Texts: Ezekiel 18:4; Leviticus 17:11; Matthew 26:26-28; 2 Co-rinthians 5:21; Galatians 3:13; Acts 4:12

God as Supreme Deity demands holiness. He never demands anything except what He Himself supplies, providing all things needed to make it pos-sible. To disobey this law of holiness brings death to the body and the soul. Jesus died in our place to save us from eternal death and give us eternal life.

In the previous lesson, we studied the priesthood of Christ. Today we look deeper into the sacrifice that He offered as High Priest. What did it ac-complish? It is impossible to cover so vast a subject in one lesson, but let us look at some of the high points.
MEMORY VERSE: For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit. —1 Peter 3:18
Atonement Is Needed

Ezekiel 18:4 All souls are mine. This statement was made truthfully by God. God is the Supreme Deity, and man is His creation. For these reasons, He has complete authority over man. He rightly sets the standard for man. God's character is holiness, and He requires holiness in man. He required obedience of Adam. He said to Abraham, "Walk before me, and be thou perfect"; and to us, He says, "Be ye holy; for I am holy" (Genesis 17:1; 1 Peter 1:16). Failure to reach God's standards brings a penalty.

The soul that sinneth, it shall die. Adam was the first to receive this law. "For in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die" (Genesis 2:17). This is a changeless law reaching from beginning to end. "The wages of sin is death" (Romans 6:23). The final and eternal sentence to sinners is "the second death" (Revelation 20:14). Since "all have sinned," this is a universal disobedience (Romans 3:23). Unless a remedy can be found, all will be lost.

Leviticus 17:11 It is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul. The life is in the blood. Life must pay for sin. "Without shedding of blood is no remission" (Hebrews 9:22). Blood is sacred. Under the Law, God accepted the blood of animals sacrificed by priests on the altar as a temporary atonement for sins. The shedding of that blood was a type of the
later shedding of Christ's blood on the Cross as the perfect Atonement (Hebrews 9:14). Here is the remedy by which all may be saved from the sins that damn the souls of mankind.
Complete Atonement

Matthew 26:26-28 For this is my blood of the new testament. Jesus and His disciples had partaken of the Passover. Although the disciples themselves did not know it, the old spiritual dispensation was being closed out, and a new one was coming into reality. Jesus did not destroy the old form; He fulfilled it. He took away the shadow and left the real thing. Under the old covenant, animal blood had to be sacrificed. To bring in this new covenant, the blood of the Son of God was the sacrifice for man's sins. A new plan would now be in force that would bring complete atonement.

This is my blood ... shed for many ... not for Himself, for He had no sin. He gave it for others, for the remission of their sins. This new covenant marks the departure of man from his imperfect, sinful state into that spiritual perfection which God has made possible for him in Jesus Christ, His only begotten Son. Moses led the children of Israel out of the bondage of Pharaoh; Jesus leads the whole world out of the bondage of Satan.

The bread and wine are significant, not only because they represent the body and blood of Christ but because bread contains every element found in the human body, and the wine represents the blood poured out, which sealed the covenant for man's redemption. This same covenant is extended to us, but we must accept it. With our finite minds, we cannot understand it. We cannot understand how God can save us or why He should care to save us. But there stands the covenant, sealed by the blood of Jesus (1 John 1:7).
Jesus Became a Cure

2 Corinthians 5:21 For he hath made him to be sin for us. Jesus had to stoop way down to obtain our freedom from eternal death. All the way from Heaven to Earth. All the way from holiness to sin. He, "the just," died for us, "the unjust, that he might bring us to God" (1 Peter 3:18).

Galatians 3:13 Christ was made a curse for us. The cross or tree was cursed (Deuteronomy 21:22-23). It was the curse for sin. Jesus voluntarily hung on the tree and so became a cursed thing. All are placed under the curse of sin. It was in place of us, to bear our curse, that He hung there. In taking our sins upon Himself, He became sin for us.
The Only Atonement

Acts 4:12 There is none other name than Jesus whereby we must be saved. There is no use in looking to any organization, form, sacrifice, suffering, good works, or any other thing to save us. Jesus died to give us life. In Him, and Him alone, our sins are paid for. To receive the benefit, we must identify with Him. We must repent of sin, take up our cross, and die to self and sin. Thus, we are "made conformable unto his death" (Philippians 3:10). As we accept Him as our sacrifice, He will give us His life. Was it enough for an Israelite to know that a lamb had been slain? No, there was more. He must have the blood applied and do all of God's commandments.
JUST A THOUGHT
It is impossible to have faith over disobedience.

blocks.text: LESSON 7
JESUS IS KING
Scripture Texts: Isaiah 9:6-7; Luke 1:30-33; Matthew 28:18; John 18:36; Matthew 12:28; 1 Corinthians 15:24-26

Many are looking for Jesus to set up an earthly kingdom here and reign from Jerusalem for a thousand years. This does not fit with the time of His kingdom as given in the Bible. It does not suit the nature of His kingdom. If the kingdom reign is to take place in the future, then kingdom blessings would also be meant for the future and not now. This is a great mistake, in which there is great harm. It causes mankind to look and wait for a ship that will never come in.
Jesus Christ is King over all. His kingdom is unseen, inside the heart, spiritual and eternal. He reigns over all. All people owe Him love, loyalty, respect, and obedience.
MEMORY VERSE: Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him. —Matthew 2:2
A King Foretold and Sent
Isaiah 9:6-7 Isaiah the prophet received from God this promise of a King. The One to come has authority to govern, is a Prince with a throne and a kingdom. His government is increasing and endless.

Luke 1:30-33 About seven hundred years later, the angel Gabriel spoke to a maiden in Nazareth of this Son of the Highest. He was to have a throne and reign over an endless kingdom. His throne is the throne of his father David. (See 1 Chronicles, Chapter 17.) He was born to Mary. He was called J ESUS (meaning Savior) as Gabriel had instructed. When a little later the wise men from the east came to worship Jesus, they asked for "he that is born King of the Jews" (Matthew 2:2). Included in this was the fact that this Baby Jesus was a King.
An All-Powerful King
Matthew 28:18 When Jesus was ending His stay on earth, He stated to His disciples, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. Power

and authority belong to kings. Jesus "taught them as one having authority" (Matthew 7:29). His authority was evident, in word and in action. "With authority commandeth he even the unclean spirits, and they do obey him" (Mark 1:27).
Special Characteristics of His Kingdom

John 18:36 Jesus said, My kingdom is not of this world. It is a heavenly one, unlike any other kingdom. It is not ruled from this world. Its head-quarters are in Heaven. Its boundaries cannot be drawn on a map. Its power is not from force but from the sweet influence of spiritual graces and from the great love between Jesus and His subjects. "The kingdom of God cometh not with observation." It is unseen. It "is within you"—an inward power in God's children (Luke 17:20-21).

This kingdom "is not meat and drink." One's position in it does not depend upon material things, forms, or ceremonies. It is "righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost" (Romans 14:17). Jesus was born a King, lived a King, died a King, rose a King, and is reigning as a King. He reigns as Sovereign, with absolute authority, not lim-ited by human laws or religious bodies. Jesus Proved His Authority

Matthew 12:28 Jesus said, If I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you. There is no question by what power Jesus did miracles. Jesus began His work, preaching the Gospel of the Kingdom of God. His kingdom was already in action.

The time in which these people look for Jesus to come back and save them (a future reign) will be the time
when He is coming back to judge them (the Judgment).

It is the joy of all who love "the Lamb that was slain" to count Him "worthy" of all praise and worship and obedience (Revelation 5:12). None will overdo it.

God wants men, but He does not need them; men need God, but they do not want Him.

blocks.text: LESSON 8
JESUS WAS CONSECRATED
Scripture Texts: Isaiah 50:6; 2 Corinthians 8:9; John 10:17-18; John 17:18-19; Matthew 26:39, 53-54; Romans 5:19; Hebrews 12:2

Jesus Christ did a marvelous work in this world when He through Himself made a way for sinners to be saved and reach Heaven. Before He came to do that work, a decision had to be made. He did not have to come. He did not have to die. He decided to do it. In unity with the Father and the Holy Spirit, He committed (or dedicated) Himself to the project of the plan of salvation for mankind.
MEMORY VERSE: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends. —John 15:13
His Sanctification

Isaiah 50:6 I gave my back to the smiters ... my cheeks ... my face. Isaiah prophesied of this part of Christ's consecration. Jesus GAVE. He was not forced. He consecrated Himself to suffer. This prophecy is fulfilled in Matthew 26:47 to 27:50.

2 Corinthians 8:9 He was rich ... he became poor. We can only vaguely picture the vastness of this move. We have never seen the riches of Heaven. He voluntarily left it all to come to a world made destitute by the poverty of sin. That ye ... might be rich. What immeasurable love! The Creator gave all to help His rebelling creation. Why did He not just scrap it as we would a cracked dish? Because of love. He had put immortal existence into His creatures and could not bear for them to spend it in Hell. Ye know the grace. Christ put into action His principle of grace—the outpouring from divine life without charge—to benefit mankind (a free gift).
He Gave His Life

John 10:17-18 Jesus came knowing He would die for mankind. It was His choice. He lived a human life. He died a human death, a shameful death, "even the death of the cross" (Philippians 2:8). He did this by His own will and commitment. Jesus had His freedom of choice.
John 17:18-19 As thou hast sent me. His coming was the joint plan of

the Trinity. For their sakes—all are invited to be saved and to have a part. He gave Himself, set Himself apart for this one purpose. Sanctified through the truth. The sanctifying agent God uses is His Word—God's message set forth in the Bible to guide every yielded heart. The world has its own methods of improvement. Never has humanity been so bent on improving itself as now. But society puts its trust in politics, human goodness, social and racial tolerance, and better living conditions. All these are commendable, but they are roots that bring forth bitter fruit.

All sound human improvement must start with the truth—God's message spoken by the Holy Spirit to the open, hungry heart. Christ sanctified Himself for us; we must sanctify ourselves for others. We must be sanctified by the acceptance of divine truth. There is no other basis for human improvement but through obedience of God's Word unto salvation. All other schemes will prove ineffective.
Victory

Matthew 26:39 Jesus' human nature shrank from suffering the Cross. His divine nature overcame the flesh. He obeyed what the Father and He had agreed upon. O my Father ... nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt. Jesus' prayer meant God's will must be done, and He intended to do it with all His heart, mind, and strength. Once a man has taken this attitude, the suffering for the cause of Jesus takes on a new and different aspect. When the purpose to glorify and demonstrate the power of God grips one's soul, suffering loses its pain and power to defeat him.

Matthew 26:53-54 Twelve legions of angels were at His command. Had He decided to return to Heaven and let the world go, He could have done so. That would have voided the many former prophecies promising salvation. His love did not allow Him to do that.

Romans 5:19 By one man's disobedience—that is, Adam's—many were made sinners. The blight of sin and death that fell on all mankind brought grief to the heart of God. Because the Father loved the world, He gave His Son. The Son loved likewise and gave Himself in obedience to God's plan in order that sinners might be made righteous. Because of His obedience, the whole glorious New Testament became a reality. God proved His love for the world by giving His Son. We show our love to God by believing and keeping His commandments (John 14:15, 23-24).

Hebrews 12:2 For the joy ... endured the cross ... is set down at the right hand of the throne of God. This is the crowning of complete victory. Jesus did not win this victory for Himself alone. It was for many. It was not

easy. "He hath poured out his soul unto death. He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied" (Isaiah 53:10-12). When He said, "It is finished" (John 19:30), it was victory, and He gained His possession. He was rewarded with a seat with His "Father in his throne" (Revelation 3:21). We, too, can be overcomers. Repent, confess our sins, take Jesus as our Sacrifice, die to self, and yield all to the leadership of the Holy Spirit. "If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me" (Matthew 16:24).
JUST A THOUGHT
People seldom lose their salvation by a blowout; usually it's just a slow leak.

blocks.text: LESSON 9
JESUS IS THE BRIDEGROOM
Scripture Texts: Romans 7:4; Ephesians 5:23-32; Revelation 19:7-9

God created man in His own image. He gave man a nature, faculties, rela-tionships, and characteristics similar to His own. This is almost too great for us to realize. One step in this was to establish the family—a man, a wife, and children joined in a functioning unit. Our earthly family is a reflection of the divine union of Christ and His church. Throughout the Bible, Jesus is often referred to as the Bridegroom: "He that hath the bride is the bridegroom: but the friend of the bridegroom ... rejoiceth greatly because of the bridegroom's voice" (John 3:29).

Because of love, Christ died for the church, cleansed her, and made her His bride, His body. As the bride, the church loves, obeys, and serves Christ, her Head. Today, we study some teachings about Christ and His church as a husband-and-wife relationship.
MEMORY VERSE: For thy Maker is thine husband; the L ORD of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel; The God of the whole earth shall he be called. —Isaiah 54:5
The Church Married to Christ

Romans 7:4 When Christ died, we were made dead to the law, that is, not under obligation to keep the Law of Moses, not married to the old Law any longer. A better, perfect law has taken its place (Hebrews 7:19). Now we are to be married ... to him who is raised from the dead, Jesus Christ. The purpose of this marriage is to bring forth fruit unto God. The fruit God desires is "the fruit of the Spirit" (Galatians 5:22-23). It is borne in the hearts of those married to Christ. Then, they bring others to be part of His bride and bear spiritual fruit also. Thus, the fruit multiplies.
The Church Subject to Christ

Ephesians 5:23-24 Similar to a human husband and wife, Christ is the head, and the church is to obey Him, be subject unto Him. This is not a one-way street. The basis for this is His love for the church, which sets the standard. This is not a subjection forced upon us by fear, but the loving com-

pliance of weakness with strength, of ignorance with wisdom, of love answering love. It is harmony and fulfillment. Wives should obey their hus-bands as the church obeys Christ. Husbands should love their wives as Christ loves the church.
Jesus Loves His Church

Ephesians 5:25-27 The basis for every true marriage is love. Christ also loved the church. Because He loves her, He wants her for His own. The church is His flesh and body (1 Corinthians 12:27). Adam's wife was from his body, part of himself, his flesh and bone. Christ's wife is also His body.

Because of love for the church, Christ gave himself for it to sanctify and cleanse it from sin. The cleansing or washing is the first step in preparing for Christ to move into our lives and abide with us. The objective of Christ in dying for His bride is to make for Himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing (morally and spiritually clean) ... holy and without blemish. No sin—sin blemishes lives. Sin can be removed by the blood of Jesus, but the scar is left permanently. His joy is to do this; hers is to have it done, to cooperate with and yield to Him.

Ephesians 5:28-32 We are members of his body ... flesh ... bones. Jesus and His redeemed ones have the closest possible relationship. Having made them holy, Jesus lives in them, and they in Him (John 14:20; 15:4). Through this close relationship, children are brought forth into the kingdom. He nourishes the church with spiritual food, life, and ability. She is His hands and feet and voice to do His work. And they two shall be one flesh. Verse 31 is a quotation of Genesis 2:24. Spiritually the one flesh takes on a much broader and deeper unity than that which is merely physical.

Centuries before Jesus came to earth, God revealed to Isaiah this union of Jesus and His church (Isaiah 54:5). The relationship of husband and wife is the closest earth knows. God gave it as a permanent earthly commitment, not to be dissolved as long as both live. Likewise, it is God's will that the relationship of the heavenly Bridegroom and His bride continue forever. Only spiritual death can separate Christ and His bride.
Love—the Basis for Marriage

Because of love for the church, Jesus died. For love, He took her as His bride. Love is the strongest of bonds. A successful marriage is built on love. Love is not shattered by inconvenience, hardship, or problems. Divorce is prevalent these days. Many fail to recognize both the necessity of love. They
also fail to understand the difference between infatuation and love and between lust and love. The object of love is the good of the loved one, not of one's self.

As there are avenues of interest and accomplishment open to the working together of husband and wife, so with Christ and the church there are great purposes to be fulfilled. We must know His purposes and be ready to fill our place as His body here on earth. It is a service of love. Marriage is a beginning, not an end.

Revelation 19:7-9 Picture the glorious marriage supper of the Lamb and the church—Jesus the conquering, Omnipotent Lord of all, the Bridegroom, taking to Himself His bride dressed in fine linen, clean and white ... the righteousness of saints. This is the grand consummation of the love and commitment of the saints and Jesus Christ to each other. This is the goal Jesus desired enough to die for. The saints desire it enough to give up all else for it. Joyful hope has a large place in earthly weddings. The union of saints with Christ includes more than joy. Along the path trials, temptations, sacrifice, suffering, and persecution may be met. How will we meet them? What part does Christ have in meeting them?
JUST A THOUGHT
A guilty conscience is a restless bedfellow.

blocks.text: LESSON 10
JESUS IS OUR GOOD SHEPHERD (PART 1)
Scripture Text: John 10:1-6

Jesus used familiar scenes or customs to illustrate His teachings. Around Him in the fields of Palestine, many flocks of sheep could be seen, cared for by shepherds. He used these to picture His relationship with His people. He called Himself the Shepherd, and the people of God, sheep.

Jesus is our Shepherd; saints are His sheep. He knows, saves, protects, feeds, and heals them. They know and follow Him. Today we study the rela-tionship between the Good Shepherd and His sheep. The background of this lesson is in Ezekiel, Chapter 34.
MEMORY VERSE: And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd. —John 10:16
Nature of the True Shepherd

John 10:1-2 The sheepfold of that day was not a building but an open en-closure. Its walls were covered with branches of thorny shrubs to keep preda-tors out. Sometimes there was a door, and at other times the shepherd himself would lie across the entrance at night, keeping his flock safe within. Several flocks occupied the same fold. Each group had names. One shepherd watched the flocks at night. In the morning, the other shepherds came and, standing outside, called their sheep by name. As the sheep began to come out of the fold, the shepherds would lead them until each flock had been led to pasture. Every shepherd knew his sheep, and each sheep knew its shepherd's voice. They could never be deceived by the voice, call, or dress of anyone else.

How beautifully this describes for all time the relationship of Christ to His church and the relationship of pastors to their flocks. He that entereth not by the door ... the same is a thief and a robber. The Pharisees were false shepherds—thieves and robbers. They had not entered in by the door. They had secured their position by political conspiracy with the Roman government. Christ was the true Shepherd, for He had been placed by God. His coming had long been prophesied. God's approval and power rested upon Him. The true sheep—men and women of genuine religious faith—heard His voice, understood Him, and followed Him.
One Voice

John 10:3-5 And the sheep hear his voice ... and leadeth them out. The shepherd goes before his sheep. This is a perfect application to Jesus, Who is our Leader in the matter of leading. He does not drive us but walks ahead of us in hours of temptation. He is near to us in seasons of pain and trouble. He goes before us in everything pertaining to this life and also to eternal life.

The sheep follow him: for they know his voice. There are many voices around us today speaking words of spiritual instruction and advice. How can we know which voice is the right voice? The Holy Spirit is the answer; He came to guide us in all things (John 16:13). Try the spirit and see where it is leading! Only the Spirit of Christ will lead us to green pastures. All others will lead to a dry, thirsty, and barren land away from God (1 John 4:1-3). Christ is telling us here that the true church must have true leaders. For they know not the voice of strangers. As the sheep only move at the voice of their shepherd, so the true saint knows no other voice but that of Jesus Christ.
A Parable

John 10:6 This parable spake Jesus unto them: but they understood not what things ... he spake unto them. Jesus told these men, no one enters the kingdom except through Him. He has not entered into the fold by the door but has attempted to climb up some other way. Why could they not understand His Words?

Israel began with God's blessing upon it. God had established it, had pro-vided in detail for its every need, and had made clear its everyday duties. But that religious body had become corrupt. The Pharisees were false shepherds—thieves and robbers. They refused to enter in by the door. Jesus tried to get them to see their condition, to find their location, and to walk in the light. But they understood not what ... he spake unto them. Their hearts were not open to receive the truth. Their traditions, seats of power, and recognition among the people caused a great number of them to fail to follow the voice of the Good Shepherd Who came to lead them out of their terrible condition into a rich experience in a new and better land, the Kingdom of God. Jesus, from that time until the present, has swept leaders of this world and their followers from their places of power by His simple, righteous teachings about the Kingdom of God.
When Christ calls and His sheep refuse to follow that call, it is only a matter of time until they, whether they be sheep or undershepherd, will be

devoured by some of the predators who wait for an opportunity to destroy the flock of Christ. The safest place is close to the Shepherd. The wolf attacks those sheep who wander away to the outside edges of the pasture.
JUST A THOUGHT
To try to win the world by the methods of the world is to become like the world.

blocks.text: LESSON 11
JESUS IS OUR GOOD SHEPHERD (PART 2)
Scripture Text: John 10:7-15, 27-28

In the last lesson, we studied the parable that Jesus gave to the Pharisees. These religious men were so bound by tradition that they could not understand the words of Jesus. Today we study, in some detail, the expla-nation that Jesus gave them concerning the Parable of Christ the Good Shepherd and His sheep.
MEMORY VERSE: For ye were as sheep going astray; but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls. —1 Peter 2:25
Jesus Is the Door

John 10:7-9 Jesus said, I am the door of the sheep. Here Jesus makes it plain that He is the door—the way into the Kingdom of God, the true fold of salvation (John 14:6). He is also the door to keep enemies out. No enemy can overcome Him to get at the sheep to destroy them. He is the only door. All others pretending to be the way to Heaven or to bring the truth are thieves and robbers. ONLY by Jesus can anyone be saved from sin and death. When we enter in by Him, we are on the inside, looking out. We belong and can enjoy and experience the good things found there.

As a shepherd leads his flock out to pasture and into rest, so Jesus leads His sheep. He knows what His people need and has placed it in His Word. He knows when they need rest or revival or encouragement. He gives it through His Word sent to us by the undershepherd, the pastor. Jesus sees our wounds and binds and heals them. He brings comfort to broken hearts. Christ and the door into the kingdom are one and the same. There are not two entrances. "Joining" is climbing up another way. It puts you into a deno-minational fold but not the fold of Christ. You cannot "join" the fold of Christ; all must enter by the door, Jesus Christ. You do not enter full-grown but healthy and ready to grow.
Life and Death
John 10:10-11 Jesus contrasted Himself with the devil and his agents. The devil promises to give much, but he has nothing to give. His only

intention is to take from us all that is good, to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. Jesus came to give, not to take. I am come that they might have life ... more abundantly. Entering by Jesus gives life to the soul. He gives life, full and rich. Because He loves them, He proves Himself a Good Shepherd; He giveth his life for the sheep. The sheep are His own; His object is their good. All He asks of them is due honor, thanks, and praise.
False Shepherds

John 10:12-13 But he that is an hireling, and not the shepherd ... leaveth the sheep, and fleeth ... wolf ... scattereth the sheep. An agent of Satan will hire out to pastor a church, teach in a school, or write a book, but he does it for the money, not for the good of the sheep. The sheep are not his; their welfare means nothing to him. When danger or need comes along he offers no help. He has none to give. Because he is an hireling—he is into the work only as a means of livelihood, the hireling fleeth—he runs away and leaves the sheep to be killed or scattered.
The True Shepherd

John 10:14-15 I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep. He knows who they are. He knows all about each one. He knows their desires, weaknesses, and needs. He knows, understands, and cares. The fact that Jesus knows His sheep is of vital value in many ways. One important way concerns the boundary line of the Church of God, the line that separates those who are saved and those who are not. Christ keeps the record. Need we another? No! Men draw lines based upon many things. "Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his" (2 Timothy 2:19). And am known of mine. This completes the rewarding association. To know Him is to love Him, to possess Him, and to have eternal life. When we know Jesus, there will be no mistaking the voice of any other to lead us astray.
Can We Leave the Fold?

John 10:27-28 My sheep hear my voice ... they follow me. This is an amazing statement to people who have been taught that we cannot be free from sin in this life. Sinners are not saints! Saints do not sin! Jesus says they follow me.
I give unto them eternal life. The song entitled "What a Kingdom" says,
"We possess it right here when He saves from all sin, And 'twill last while the ages shall roll."

Neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. No enemy (nothing) is strong enough to snatch a saint from the flock of the all-powerful Jesus or His Father. The only one who can remove a saint from the hand of Christ is oneself. The choice is left to us, individually.

It is widely taught that "once saved, always saved," that nothing you do can bring about the loss of the salvation you once received. Yet one cannot be saved from sin and be a sinner at the same time. A sheep cannot be inside the fold and outside the fold at the same time (1 John 3:8-10). Christ keeps all who remain with Him secure, but He restrains no one by force. Anyone who chooses to depart from Him does so by crossing the line of safety into the realm of sin and Satan. (Read 2 Peter 2:20-21.) So you can fall, but what a sad day it is if you do.
JUST A THOUGHT
Error often rides to its deadly work on the back of truth (Charles Spurgeon).

blocks.text: LESSON 12
JESUS IS OUR FRIEND
Scripture Texts: John 15:9-16; Luke 12:32; Revelation 3:20; John 17:3

To unite man with Himself is the purpose of all God's dealings with man from Creation to the Resurrection and Final Judgment. Jesus Christ came to man to transact that union. His coming was sacrificial, intimate, warm, and loving. Jesus came in love, understanding, and sympathy. He opens His heart and invites us to know Him so that He can show us the Father. To know Him and the Father is eternal life.
MEMORY VERSE: If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you. —John 15:7
How to Be Joyful

John 15:9-11 As the hour drew near for Jesus to die on the Cross, He was alone with His disciples. Jesus talked with them intimately and sincerely. He told them, As the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you. This love is great, strong, and lasting. It is the basis for all other love. Again and again, Jesus emphasized His love for His disciples, but here He compares His love to that which the Father had for Him. The disciples should continue in it by living in it. They could do this only by obedience to His commands. Obedience is the key to all the riches of Christ. By obedience, Jesus Himself remained in the Father's love (John 8:29).

The thought that underlies Jesus' speech in these last hours (about dwell-ing in Christ, in His joy, in His words, and in His peace) is that of a safe dwelling place, a safe house, into which we enter and may be secure. Here, all that continue in it find a fortress from sorrow, care, trouble, and temptation. His love shields us from whatever befalls us. We can sing: "He hideth my soul in the cleft of the rock ... and covers me there with His hand." By continuing in His love, we can have joy abiding and full, His joy that is greater than any joy the world knows—"unspeakable and full of glory" (1 Peter 1:8). Jesus wants our joy and happiness to be full. The thought of these verses is this: What the Father was to Jesus, He would be to His disciples.
John 15:12-13 Jesus commands nothing impossible. He commands us to love as He loves. We can do it only if we have His love and power. His love
placed in a human heart enables that man or woman to love as He loves. Jesus loved enough to die for both friends and enemies. An enemy who accepts His sacrifice becomes His friend.
Friends of Jesus

John 15:14-16 Ye are my friends. A great and high privilege! But there is a condition: If ye do whatsoever I command you. Jesus proves His friendship by disclosing His knowledge and plans to us and by choosing us to bear fruit for Him and to receive answers to prayer. Because the fruit we bear is divine in origin, it remains or is permanent. Jesus, our Friend, opens His storehouse of blessings to those who go forth obeying and bringing forth fruit,

Luke 12:32 Fear not, little flock. Jesus used this term as a fond parent speaks to loved children—familiar and intimate. It is your Father's ("your" rather than "my" this time) good pleasure (He enjoys the giving, which indicates the quality and quantity of His love) to give you the kingdom. He wants all humanity to have this gift—the rule of God in the heart.
There is a remedy for the great lack of joy and happiness. Thanks and praise be unto God! The love and friendship of Jesus enable us to be happy in the midst of illness, poverty, trouble, or loss.

We are told in 1 John 3:2, when we see God as He is, we will be like Him. We see God when we meet Jesus, His Son. The better we know Jesus, the more like God we become. This knowledge is brought about through prayer, Bible study, and spiritual leaders who are given by God to assist (Ephesians 4:13). You must first enter Christ before there can be an increase in knowledge of Him (1 Corinthians 2:14). How do you enter?
Results of Knowing Jesus

Revelation 3:20 Jesus said to John, I stand at the door, and knock. He is the polite Visitor, seeking entrance to the most private, personal place of a person—his heart. He waits to be invited in. I will ... sup with him, and he with me. We have here a picture of close friends in a warm, satisfying relationship, honoring each other as host and Guest. Thus, Jesus draws near to His friends—any who open their hearts to Him. Oh, what sweet commu-nion this brings to the friends of Jesus!

John 17:3 Life eternal, begun and enjoyed here and now, is the final treasure all desire to find at the end of earth's years. Most will fail. A few will reach it. How? By knowing God the Father and His Son, Jesus,

and abiding in them. This reveals the exceeding importance of knowing Him. It is not merely to know ABOUT Him, but to KNOW Him—to be acquainted with Him and to experience a personal relationship with Him. He wants to do a work in us, so that we can know Him as He knows us. We reach this through repentance, believing in Him, and following Him. Then we can rightfully say, "I know Him; I have eternal life."
JUST A THOUGHT
No one is a failure in this world who lightens a burden for someone else.

blocks.text: LESSON 13
JESUS IS OUR MEDIATOR
Scripture Texts: Hebrews 2:9-18; Ephesians 4:13-15; 1 Timothy 2:5

For mankind to find joy and satisfaction with God, man must be joined with Him in a permanent union. Man is bound to God by having His nature, tastes, habits, and purposes. He must have His quality and likeness.

It was and is God's intent to unite Himself with man. This He accom-plished in Jesus Christ, our Lord and Savior. How it is done—what it means and what it will accomplish in each one—is a sphere of thought too great and marvelous for our earthly minds to take in. But we can look in, enter and walk with our hands in His, trusting Him to lead us into complete unity with the Father.

MEMORY VERSE: And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testa-ment, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance. —Hebrews 9:15
A Mediator Needed
A mediator is one who intercedes. He is a conciliator between persons or sides.

Hebrews 2:9-10 The writer had just been speaking of men and angels. Then he turned to consider Jesus. Jesus Christ the Son of God is the highest plane of existence, the highest life. Yet He came down past the plane of His created angels, on down a little lower to the plane of sinning man. He did it freely because of His great love for lost mankind. He became man for a purpose. It was to taste death for every man. God cannot die. To die, Jesus had to become man.

Man received the sentence of death when sin came in (Genesis 2:17; 3:19; Romans 5:12). So Jesus became man to take man's place in death. For it became him, was fitting for Him. It was the only way from the depths to the highest. Through suffering, He brought perfection to man. He takes with Him many sons unto glory because He first went down far enough to reach them—us.
Basis for Unity

Hebrews 2:11-13 For both ... are all of one. Christ and His redeemed people are joined together in one body. As Jesus said to the Father, "I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one" (John 17:23). And as Paul wrote to the saints at Colosse, "For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God" (Colossians 3:3). Jesus joined us in quality. Jesus is pure and holy. He sanctifies or makes His people holy like Himself. He puts in them His life and nature. He makes them partakers of the divine nature. He identifies with His one people. He seals them with "that holy Spirit of promise" (Ephesians 1:13). The Holy Spirit lives in them to teach, guide, empower, and shine. He fills the heart with the love of God (Romans 5:5). These sanctified brethren of Christ live like Him because they are united with Him. Because they share the same life, he is not ashamed to call them brethren. Jesus acknowledges His saints. He owns the Father before them; He owns them before the Father. He takes His place as one of them, unashamed.
Jesus Partook of Flesh and Blood

Hebrews 2:14-18 As the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also. To substitute for man He must be man with all that flesh and blood includes—human nature, joy, sorrow, weakness, weariness, hunger, thirst, pain, death. Above all, it was death He came to take. Why? For love, that He could be our Mediator, that missing link needed to bring lost mankind back to God (Romans 8:34; Hebrews 7:25; 9:15, 24). His love shines through these Scriptures. It was to bring sons unto God's glory, to sanctify them, to destroy the devil's power over them in temptation, to free them from fear of death, to redeem them from sin. As our Mediator, He is able to make reconciliation with God for our sins. Because he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted.
Grow Up

Ephesians 4:13-15 Jesus became one of us that we may become one with Him. The goal of the program He set in motion is to bring man to the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ: That we ... may grow up into him in all things. He will, if we let Him, make us like Him and part of Him. This blessed union is planned to continue eternally. The Church of God is the union of God and man linked together by Jesus Christ. Christ is the
Head, and saints are the body; or Christ is the Vine, and saints are the branches. Life cannot flow without this union.
Only One Way of Union

1 Timothy 2:5 For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus. As Mediator, Jesus joins God and man. To experience this blessed, holy, happy union, we must go through Jesus. We must repent, believe on, and follow Him.
